messages:
michael: Heads-up — prod-usw3 warm-pool join failures started ~00:10 UTC after the permission-boundary rollout. Nodes get as far as provisioning but fail attestation and never send audit events. Warmers stuck: 18 pending.

infra-bot: ALERT 1839990001 - warm-pool-join x18 failed in prod-usw3. Errors: sts:AssumeRoleDenied (permission boundary), s3:PutObjectAccessDenied (audit put), eni_attach_timeout.

olga: I see the permission boundary patch intended for the maintenance role accidentally attached to infra-allocator role via `apply -target=aws_iam_role_policy_attachment` during the rollout. That boundary denies s3:PutObject to our secure-audit bucket unless request principal has tag env=ops. Allocator sessions don't have that tag.

sven: So two knock-on effects: (1) allocator can't AssumeRole into hsm-proxy because boundary blocks sts:AssumeRole; (2) node-agent can't write attestation to s3://secure-audit because PutObject is denied (and PutObject is KMS-encrypted, so it also surfaces as kms:Encrypt failing downstream).

policy-bot: Policy diff flagged: added boundary `pb-restrict-eu-priv` attached to role=infra-allocator in prod-usw3 by change set ch-2026-04-01-xx. Recommend immediate detach for recovery.

michael: We need a fix that doesn't expand scope broadly. Options: A) detach the boundary from infra-allocator in prod-usw3 only (fast, targeted); B) add a short-lived session tag env=ops when allocator assumes role (requires code change); C) fallback warmup to prod-usw1 (costly). Thoughts?

olga: A is fastest. We should record an explicit audit entry and require postmortem about why the boundary was attached incorrectly. I'll prepare a terraform rollback targeting the single attachment and include automated approval audit.

sven: Note: if we detach boundary, nodes will start joining but we must also ensure the KMS grant used for attestation hasn't been revoked during the window. I'm seeing a few grants with creation_time ~00:05 UTC; need to verify validity.

infra-bot: ACTION: creating incident INC-20260401-01, owner=michael, priority=P1. Will surface policy diff and related runbook steps.

julia: Security + compliance: prefer A with controls: (1) detach only in prod-usw3 and tag the change with `approval=oncall+sec` in terraform, (2) push a one-time acceptance flag to approvals service, (3) require immediate audit export of all role bindings for last 24h to s3://secure-audit/incident-1839990001/. I can standby to sign off.

michael: Doing detach now: `terraform apply -target=aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.allocator-pb-detach -var='env=prod-usw3' -auto-approve` — will follow with approval note.

infra-bot: UPDATE: detach applied. Requeueing warmers. Status: requeued 18; joined 7/18; 11 retrying.

olga: While detach helps, we also need to make attestation writes resilient to KMS key rotation. The root cause trace shows the node-agent tried to PutObject with encryption context missing `purpose=hsm-attest` and the KMS key policy rejected it. We should add an intermediate retry that fetches the active grant id before uploading.

sven: Agreed. I'll open a small PR to node-agent: fetch latest grant metadata from our key-rotation service and include encryptionContextSubset when calling PutObject/KMS encrypt. Also add a retry with backoff for PutObject 403->refresh tokens.

julia: Compliance asks for an immediate export of all PutObject failures to the incident bucket and a signed attestation that we won't leave the detach permanent. I'll add a 2-hour TTL guard: auto-reattach boundary if incident not closed and manual review not completed.

finance-bot: Cost note if fallback used: routing 18 nodes to prod-usw1 would be ~3.6TB/day => est $600/day egress. Also alert: frequent warmup retries increase reserved capacity burn.

michael: Warmers currently stabilizing. Final status at 00:55 UTC: 18/18 joined. Recording action items here: (1) olga - PR to add session-tag option and improve retry for PutObject (2) sven - PR to node-agent to refresh grant metadata and encryptionContext handling (3) julia - post-incident audit export + governance for permission boundary rollout (4) infra - add preflight check in rollout pipeline to detect accidental role attachments.

olga: Attached quick repro snippet for pipeline preflight (sanitized):
```
# preflight: ensure policy boundaries only target maintenance roles
changed_attachments=$(git diff --name-only $CHANGES | grep aws_iam_role_policy_attachment || true)
for a in $changed_attachments; do
  role=$(jq -r '.resource.role' $a)
  if [[ "$role" == "infra-allocator" ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: attaching boundary to infra-allocator detected"; exit 1
  fi
done
```

sven: I'll also add a monitoring alert: high rate of s3:PutObjectAccessDenied from node-agent -> auto-block rollout and open incident.

julia: Compliance note: we'll require the team to run a tabletop for permission boundary rollouts and include a checklist item to exclude production allocator/service roles.

infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: incident INC-20260401-01 resolved; monitor window 2h. Audit export saved to s3://secure-audit/incident-1839990001/export.json.

michael: Thanks team. We'll do a short blameless postmortem tomorrow; tagging owners on action items. :thumbsup:
